_meta._note: Wave 9 — Matbench Discovery leaderboard ingest. Strict primary-source attribution: every (model_id, benchmark_id, value) triple is visible on https://matbench-discovery.materialsproject.org/ leaderboard table (data-sort-value attributes for F1 and MAE columns, scraped 2026-05-09). Mappings to DB model IDs: berkeley/chgnet→CHGNet (chgnet-0.3.0 row), cambridge/mace-mp-0→MACE-MP-0, deepmind/gnome→GNoME, meta/equiformer-v2→eqV2 M (eqV2-m-omat-salex-mp, the canonical EquiformerV2 entry by Meta FAIR), microsoft/mattersim→MatterSim v1 5M, orbital-materials/orb-v2→ORB v2, orbital-materials/orb-v3→ORB v3. Skipped: deepmodeling/dpa-2 (leaderboard only has DPA-3.1 variants, different model generation; no DPA-2 row), harvard/nequip (leaderboard has multiple retrained NequIP variants — Nequip-MP-L/OAM-L/OAM-XL — but DB id is generic so attribution to a specific variant is ambiguous), meta/uma-omat24 (not on leaderboard), microsoft/mattergen (generative model, not evaluated on Matbench Discovery F1/MAE). The mattergen_yield benchmark was NOT created because the Nature MatterGen paper (s41586-025-08628-5) main text reports only RELATIVE comparisons ('60% more SUN', '70% increase') and individual component percentages (52% unique at 10M, 61% novel) but no single absolute 'SUN yield %' figure. Per strict-attribution rule, no extrapolation. Matbench Discovery method paper: https://www.nature.com/articles/s42256-025-01055-1.

benchmarks.name: Matbench Discovery (F1)
benchmarks.description: Matbench Discovery — F1 score on stable-vs-unstable classification of WBM test set crystals (energy above hull). Higher is better. Leaderboard at matbench-discovery.materialsproject.org.

benchmarks.name: Matbench Discovery (MAE)
benchmarks.description: Matbench Discovery — Mean Absolute Error (eV/atom) on formation-energy-per-atom prediction over WBM test set. Lower is better.
